C1.worst_defect: The hero speaks to the freelancer, not the shop: 'Your own store needs the plugin on your Vendure server first' is the first instruction. Nothing above the fold says what the counter needs (a computer with Chrome, a card terminal you already have, a printer) or whether app.vendurepos.com costs anything.
C1.where: home.desktop.01 / home.phone.01, hero and CTA line

C2.worst_defect: Device support is vague for a counter decision. The page says only 'Its browser tests run in desktop Chrome; other browsers are not tested yet', so an owner can't tell whether the iPad or Android tablet at the counter will work tomorrow.

C3.worst_defect: The quick start is complete and ends with a good 'Check it worked' list. But it runs to nine steps (migrations by tsx script, tax strategy table, CORS, permissions) with no time estimate and no hand-off line telling the freelancer what to give the shop staff once it works.

C4.worst_defect: The cashier page mixes live-demo-only features into staff instructions: 'Refund at the till (live demo)' sits beside 'Refund a sale', where a real store is told to 'Ask whoever manages your Vendure store'. Troubleshooting also shows cashiers raw errorCodes such as register_session_already_open.
C4.where: at-the-till 'Refund a sale' / 'Refund at the till (live demo)'; troubleshooting 'Till updates line'

C5.worst_defect: The cashier-sheet and closure screenshots float small inside oversized grey frames with large empty padding, so the day-close screen looks lost on the page.

C6.worst_defect: The payment screenshot takes a long stretch of scrolling on a phone before the explanatory text. Long code identifiers and inline chips wrap awkwardly on the docs pages. Nothing overflows.

C7.worst_defect: Minor only: the not-found page has no JSON-LD and logs the expected 404 resource error in the console. Lighthouse is 98/100/100/100, and llms.txt, the sitemap, robots, search and the OG image all work.

overall_worst.defect: A shop owner cannot tell whether the device at their counter will work. The only statement is 'Its browser tests run in desktop Chrome; other browsers are not tested yet', with no answer for a counter iPad, an Android tablet or a Chromebook. That is the first question for 'can staff sell with this tomorrow'.
overall_worst.fix: Add one plain line on home and at the top of Limitations naming what is known to work at a counter (for example: desktop Chrome on Windows/Mac and Chromebook tested; Android Chrome and iPad Safari not tested yet; use a desktop or laptop with Chrome for now).
